hero.title: Turn carrier substitution into one bounded commercial test.
hero.summary: A narrow path to determine whether a useful capability can survive a change of compute or model carrier — with technical depth gated by an agreed commercial basis.

situation.title: The question worth testing
body: Models, runtimes and hardware carriers change quickly. A durable system should not require its useful outcome to be redefined every time the underlying carrier changes.

The immediate opportunity is not a broad integration programme. It is a bounded demonstrator that asks one falsifiable question: can the same intended outcome and execution boundary survive a carrier substitution under agreed success criteria?

theses.title: Test the substitution, not the story
theses.body: The useful unit of evidence is a measured before-and-after test with a locked outcome, boundary and pass/fail condition.

theses.title: Separate durable outcome from replaceable carrier
theses.body: The model, runtime or hardware may change. The outcome contract and consequence boundary should remain stable enough to compare the two paths directly.

theses.title: Commercial basis before technical depth
theses.body: A serious demonstrator should establish scope, ownership, value allocation and the decision gate before additional implementation detail is exchanged.

evidence.title: Bounded evaluation method
evidence.body: VALO uses explicit baselines, locked success criteria and retained evidence so a substitution result can be accepted or rejected rather than narrated after the fact.

evidence.title: Carrier-neutral architecture principle
evidence.body: The public VALO architecture separates durable object and execution boundaries from replaceable compute and model components.

evidence.title: RETONAI-specific result remains open
evidence.body: No RETONAI-specific performance, integration or commercial claim is asserted here. Those are precisely what a bounded test would need to establish.

proposal.title: Proposed next step: define the commercial basis first
body: Agree one bounded demonstrator, the customer or workload class it represents, the baseline, the measurable success criteria and the decision that follows a pass or fail.

Before further technical material is exchanged, define the commercial basis: scope, ownership of pre-existing and newly created material, permitted use of results, value allocation and what each party contributes.
Once that gate is clear, the technical test can be specified narrowly enough to produce evidence rather than an open-ended integration effort.

questions: What single outcome would make a carrier-substitution test commercially meaningful?
Which baseline should the substituted path be compared against?
What must remain invariant across the carrier change for the result to count?
How should verified recurring value, if any, be allocated between the parties?
What technical information is actually necessary after the commercial basis is agreed?

cta.title: Define the commercial basis
cta.body: Lock scope, ownership, value allocation, contributions and the pass/fail decision gate before moving into technical implementation detail.
